# Shroom Labs

> Chamber profiles for OpenShrooly. Culinary first. Offline-first.

Site: https://shroomlabs.io

## Culinary

- [Beech / Buna Shimeji](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/beech-shimeji.html): Clustered beech mushroom. Cool, humid, and a little less FAE than oysters.
- [Blue Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/blue-oyster.html): Cool-preferring oyster. Deep color holds better below 18 °C.
- [Button / Cremini](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/button-cremini.html): Compost + casing species. Low light, cool fruiting, casing required.
- [Chestnut Mushroom](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/chestnut.html): Clustered woodlover. Cool fruiting and high RH keep caps glossy.
- [Cordyceps militaris](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/cordyceps-militaris.html): Grown on supplemented grain/rice, not logs. Wants 12/12 light once orange initials show.
- [Elm Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/elm-oyster.html): Not a true Pleurotus. Cooler fruiting, meaty single fruits more than oyster clusters.
- [Enoki](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/enoki.html): Needs cold fruiting and low FAE for supermarket-long stems.
- [Golden Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/golden-oyster.html): Warm oyster with dense golden clusters. Needs strong FAE to keep stems short.
- [King Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/king-oyster.html): Thick-stem oyster. Cooler, slightly drier, and less FAE than cluster oysters.
- [King Oyster — thick-stem method](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/king-oyster-thick-stem.html): Paid example recipe: cooler, drier fruiting to favor thick stems.
- [Lion's Mane](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/lions-mane.html): Tooth fungus. Moderate FAE — too much air yellows spines.
- [Maitake](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/maitake.html): Slow woodlover. Primordia look like brains; do not dry them out.
- [Nameko](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/nameko.html): Cool, very wet fruiting. The slime coat is normal.
- [Pearl Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/pearl-oyster.html): Forgiving beginner oyster. Fast, high FAE, cool-to-room fruiting.
- [Pink Oyster](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/pink-oyster.html): Tropical oyster. Wants warmth; stalls and fades in a cold room.
- [Pioppino](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/pioppino.html): Black poplar mushroom. Cool fruiting; keep the surface less wet than oysters.
- [Reishi](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/reishi.html): Antlers under high CO2, then consoles when FAE increases.
- [Shiitake](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/shiitake.html): Needs a full colonize + browning rest, then a cold shock before fruiting.
- [Turkey Tail](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/turkey-tail.html): Thin polypore. Long fruiting, lots of FAE, not a thick-fleshed edible.
- [Wine Cap](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/wine-cap.html): Best as an outdoor bed mushroom. Indoor profile is a climate approximation only.
- [Wood Ear](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/wood-ear.html): Warm, wet jelly fungus. High RH matters more than light intensity.

## Off-menu

Internal pack id: psilocybin. Visitor-facing name: Off-menu.

Psilocybin mushrooms are illegal to grow, possess or sell in most countries and in most US states under federal law. This information is published for educational, research and harm-reduction purposes only. Check the laws where you live. Shroom Labs does not sell spores, cultures or psilocybin products.

Spore purchase and possession laws vary by state and country. Some US states ban spores outright. Where they are sold, spores are offered for microscopy only.

- [B+](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/b-plus.html): Forgiving cubensis strain with a slightly wider temperature window.
- [Golden Teacher](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/golden-teacher.html): Common cubensis strain. Standard monotub-style climate mapped onto Shrooly setpoints.
- [Penis Envy](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/penis-envy.html): Slower cubensis. Same climate band as Golden Teacher with longer stage timers.
- [Psilocybe cyanescens](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/p-cyanescens.html): Cool-weather woodlover. Indoor chambers are a poor substitute for outdoor beds.
- [Psilocybe natalensis](https://shroomlabs.io/profiles/p-natalensis.html): Cubensis-adjacent climate; often described as a bit more vigorous.

## Microscopy and research (third-party, nofollow, no affiliate)

These are plain third-party outbound links. We do not endorse the vendors or publishers, we do not profit from them, and there are no affiliate codes or tracking parameters.

- [PNW Spore](https://pnwspore.com/) — Pacific Northwest Spore Co. (Spokane). Cubensis spore syringes and prints labeled for microscopy.
- [Sporeworks](https://sporeworks.com/) — Long-running US microscopy catalog (The Spore Works). Notes CA, ID, FL, and GA spore restrictions.
- [Johns Hopkins Center for Psychedelic and Consciousness Research](https://www.hopkinspsychedelic.org/publications) — Peer-reviewed psilocybin publications from Johns Hopkins Medicine.
